children: The court found that Garg’s prima facie role in acquiring, concealing and laundering alleged proceeds of crime was significant, and said the possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with evidence or absconding could not be ruled out.

A special court in Raipur has rejected the regular bail application of businessman Vikas Garg in a money-laundering case linked to the alleged Mahadev Online Betting operation and purported proceeds of crime amounting to Rs 940.77 crore. Special Judge under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act and Sixth Additional Sessions Judge Amit Rathore dismissed Garg’s first bail application on September 29, 2026.
Garg had sought bail under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, read with Sections 45 and 65 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
He was arrested by the Directorate of Enforcement on July 14, 2026, in connection with ECIR/RPZO/10/2022.
ED Alleges Receipt Of Rs 940.77 Crore

The Enforcement Directorate alleged that Garg, through entities under his control, received Rs 765.77 crore via Elara Capital PLC from foreign entities allegedly controlled by Hari Shankar Tibrewal, who has been linked to illegal online betting activities.

The agency further alleged that Garg and his companies directly or indirectly received approximately Rs 175 crore from shell companies controlled by alleged entry provider Amit Sarawagi, taking the total purported proceeds of crime to Rs 940.77 crore.
According to the ED, the money was received through bank accounts belonging to Garg, his family members and companies under his control.
The funds were allegedly used in the acquisition of Ebix Inc. through an entity identified in the order as M/s Eranya Lifespaces Limited.

The agency also alleged that Garg created a forged and backdated addendum dated August 16, 2024, between two entities under his control to transfer a 51 per cent shareholding in Ebix International Holdings Limited.
Properties worth Rs 940.77 crore belonging to Garg, his family and associated companies were provisionally attached by the ED on June 5, 2026.
The prosecution further alleged that Garg subsequently attempted to sell a property located at 1, Ebix Way, Johns Creek, Georgia, in the United States.
Senior Advocate Vikram Chaudhri, appearing for Garg, argued that there was no credible money trail connecting his client or associated companies with proceeds derived from illegal betting.

The defence submitted that Garg was unaware of the alleged criminal origin of the funds, had cooperated with the investigation and had not attempted to abscond. It was also argued that his statements had been obtained by threatening the arrest of his family members.

Garg sought parity with other accused persons who had been granted bail and contended that his arrest did not comply with Sections 19(1) and 19(2) of the PMLA. The defence further submitted that he was unwell and was unlikely to tamper with evidence or commit another offence if released.
Court Finds Prima Facie Significant Role
The court found prima facie material indicating Garg’s significant role in the acquisition, collection and distribution of the alleged proceeds of crime.

It observed that the alleged offence appeared to have been executed in a planned manner. Rejecting the plea for parity, the court said Garg’s alleged role in laundering a substantial amount distinguished his case from that of other accused persons.
The court also found that the requirements governing Garg’s arrest under Sections 19(1) and 19(2) of the PMLA appeared to have been complied with.
It noted that he was arrested in New Delhi and produced before the nearest court on the same day before being brought to the Raipur court pursuant to a transit remand.

“Considering the role of the main accused Vikas Garg, who is prima facie involved in the serious crime of laundering a massive amount of Rs 940.77 crore, he is not entitled to obtain the benefit of bail on the basis of the principle of parity,” the court observed.

It further held that Garg’s release could create a risk of evidence being tampered with, witnesses being influenced or the accused absconding. The underlying ECIR pertains to a Chhattisgarh Police case registered at Mohan Nagar Police Station in Durg under Sections 420 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code in connection with the alleged Mahadev Online Betting operation.
The matter is listed to stand as before on October 7, 2026.
Appearances: Senior Advocate Vikram Chaudhri, along with Advocate Mohit Kumar, appeared for Vikas Garg. Special Public Prosecutor Dr Saurabh Kumar Pandey represented the Directorate of Enforcement.
